findings.detail: A supplementary acquisition-date/cost row repeats an SOI instrument and was treated as a fair-value-bearing portfolio leaf.

rationale: Class 3 anchor triangulation reconciles: the filing reports total investments of 1,662,543,940, including money market funds of 26,887,322, leaving 1,635,656,618 for the extracted private portfolio. The B01 coverage failure is instead caused by supplementary acquisition-date/cost schedule rows being counted as leaves. BPCP Craftsman is decisive: the main SOI row at table 25 row 12 states cost 15,686 and fair value 6,738, while table 30 row 10 repeats the same instrument and cost in a schedule whose columns are only Investment, Type, Acquisition Date, and Acquisition Cost. The repeated cost-only row legitimately has no source fair value but is not a separate holding; counting it as a leaf creates the missing-fair-value population.
